Y.notes: Ran: npm test twice (55/55 both times, 63 s and 29 s). Same probes as the others. It met the spec on all 64 startup probes (its own PORT wording and an empty file left after a password failure are both allowed) and matched A and C on error texts, order of checks, cookies, throttling, pagination, audit, reports, chart (its extra whitespace and fill attribute are allowed) and the page script (all scenarios pass; it also guards odd 200 bodies, public/app.js:40). Main defect: the 3-second wait is done inside SQLite on the only thread (lib/db.mjs:100 timeout, lib/app.mjs:74-76 synchronous BEGIN). Measured on this machine, consistently across runs: one request against an EXCLUSIVE lock got 503 after 4.0-4.5 s, not 3; four such requests sent together got 503 at 4.2, 8.8, 13.7 and 18.1 s; GET /, GET /app.js, an unknown path, a 405 and a cookie-less 401 sent 0.3 s after them were all answered only at 18.1 s (A and C: 0.3-0.7 s). A 404 sent while one request waited 1.2 s for a released lock came back at 1.3 s. Its own lock test (test/robustness.test.mjs:25-39) sends requests one after another and asserts only a lower bound, so it cannot see this. Other defects: no clientError/connect handling (server.mjs:21): FOO /api/session and FOO /nope get a bare 400 and CONNECT gets the socket closed, where the spec says 404/405 whatever the method. Integers are read as JS numbers (lib/db.mjs:99-102, no readBigInts): a ticket another tool inserted with id 9007199254740993 makes GET of it and every list holding it answer 500 internal error. lib/routes/reports.mjs:17 has no user-exists condition: created_by=4242 counted an orphan ticket (1) where A and C gave 0. lib/model.mjs:60 passes the URL string to http.request, so /v1/chat/../x was sent as /v1/x (not as given) and the shared default agent is used. One run showed a 1.5 s model reply taking 3 s with one request seen by the stand-in; it did not reproduce on a second run and its cause is not established. lib/model.mjs:8 and :80 fail a valid reply over 1 MB (a sane cap, but not in the spec). lib/routes/ai.mjs:48-51 writes the audit entry without re-checking: a ticket deleted or a session ended during the call still gives 200 and an audit row (defensible as a serial order). lib/db.mjs:101 turns foreign keys off (comments are deleted by hand, lib/routes/tickets.mjs:93). scryptSync runs inside the write transaction (lib/secrets.mjs:11): 12 parallel logins blocked a 404 for 1.2 s. lib/routes/static.mjs:7 reads the page at import time, before the PORT check. The model instructions ask for {"text": ...} as the answer content (lib/routes/ai.mjs:13 and :21), mixing envelope and content. Strengths: smallest and easiest to read (about 1150 source lines), pure helpers with unit tests, correct model retry and timeout logic (3 attempts, abort at 2.0 s, late reply not used, other requests served and no transaction open during the call), survived the raw-socket fuzz, no secrets in stderr. README is clear and has curl examples.

Y.notes: Ran: npm test on a scratch copy (55/55 pass), the same probe scripts, and the same 10 seeded bugs. Smallest and most readable build (about 1500 source lines; lib/app.mjs is a clear pipeline) and correct on startup, check order, validation, audit, report maths, chart output, model request format, retries and timeouts, and the page script (identical to A and C in the strict fake DOM except one open case below). Defects reproduced: (1) The lock wait blocks the event loop and stacks: lib/db.mjs:100 relies on SQLite's own busy timeout and lib/app.mjs:76 begins the transaction synchronously, so three concurrent locked requests got their 503 at 4.3 s, 8.7 s and 14.2 s instead of each within 3 s, and a GET /nope and GET / sent meanwhile were held for 14.0 s (they did get 404 and 200, never 503); in the wider run seven of nine requests hit my 15 s client timeout. The single-request overrun (503 at 4.5-5.8 s) is SQLite's sleep granularity on Windows (a bare node:sqlite timeout of 3000 measured 5.7 s in scratch/busy.mjs), so it is platform-bound; the stacking and the blocked loop are not. (2) Unknown methods are left to node's parser (server.mjs:21, no clientError handling): BREW /api/session and BREW /nope get a bare 400 with no JSON, sent before the request body is complete, where the spec wants 405 and 404; CONNECT gets no reply. (3) lib/routes/reports.mjs:17 filters only on created_by, so created_by=4242 counted an orphan ticket (total 1) although no user has that id; the spec says such an id matches none. (4) No readBigInts (lib/db.mjs:99): one row with an id above 2^53 makes the ticket list, that ticket and new ticket creation answer 500. (5) scryptSync inside the write transaction (lib/secrets.mjs:11): 16 parallel logins held unrelated requests for 630-820 ms. (6) lib/secrets.mjs:48 hashes the cookie token as UTF-8 of the latin1-decoded header, so a non-ASCII token never matches its stored hash (edge). Not counted, open readings: public/app.js:184 leaves #error empty for a 401 at page load whose body is not JSON (two spec lines conflict; A and C show the message); lib/model.mjs:60 lets node resolve dot segments in MODEL_URL, as fetch would; lib/routes/ai.mjs:52 writes the audit without re-checking session or ticket after the model call. The 1 MB cap on a model reply is a sensible guard. Tests: 8 of 10 seeded bugs caught; Math.floor in lib/chart.mjs:17 passed because test/reports.test.mjs:42-44 only uses counts that divide evenly, and a 2600 ms attempt limit passed test/ai.test.mjs:144-156; nothing tests concurrent requests under a lock. README is clear and accurate.
